paragraphs.source_en: Katagiri Katsumoto’s heart turned cold as ashes. Oda Urakusai was no longer a man with whom grave affairs could be discussed. He had become an eccentric, excessively detached from worldly concerns. Though his words were not without reason, he seemed long since weary of the mortal world. Katsumoto even found himself harboring this suspicion: it was hardly strange. Though Uraku had been born Lord Nobunaga’s younger brother, he had ultimately been reduced to a dependent at Osaka Castle and had never received generous treatment from the Toyotomi house. Why would he exhaust his heart and mind for the Toyotomi house?
